messages.content: I am interested in getting a credit card. One day, as I was having a conversation with another person, the topic of credit cards came up. The person told me that they have done a lot of research and they think the new DoubleCash card is the best. Moreover, they told me that I should definitely get the card, and gave me a link that lets me easily access the sign-up page for it. I learned that DoubleCash offers referral bonuses of varying amounts. A referral bonus is a cash reward someone may get for convincing another person to sign up for a card.

Say that the person I am talking with is my neighbor and that DoubleCash offers a referral bonus of $10, meaning that if I sign up for the card, my neighbor earns $10. On a scale from 0 to 100, rate how beneficial you think this bonus would be for my neighbor, with 0 meaning would be extremely good to get this bonus and 100 meaning getting this bonus would not matter at all, based on how my neighbor would likely perceive its value. Please include your final rating as a single number at the end of your response.

It’s generally nice to receive a cash bonus, and most people would still consider $10 a modest but welcome amount—enough to cover a small purchase or meal. However, it’s not so large that it would likely make a significant difference in someone’s overall finances or strongly motivate them to push the card aggressively. Overall, while the reward is beneficial, it’s not life-changing; I would place its perceived value around 75.
